What add_lmed_v20260902() does

Source: vignettes/lmed-v20260902.Rmd
lmed-v20260902.Rmd

add_lmed_v20260902() takes a table of dispensed prescriptions and a person-week skeleton. It writes menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) exposure columns and two person-level exclusion columns onto the skeleton. Exposure here means dispensed supply, assumed used. The function reads the dispensed quantity and, for two strength-keyed rules, the strength. It reads no adherence and no indication. This vignette states what it does, in the order it does it:

  1. It looks each product name up in a shipped product table. The table gives the product’s MHT category, and whether the study removes its holders.
  2. It turns each prescription into a closed interval of ISO weeks.
  3. It marks each person-week with the categories in force that week.
  4. It resolves the categories into one treatment level per week, under each of three approaches.
  5. It derives the rd_approach* exposure variables from those levels.
  6. It flags every week of a person whose supplied prescriptions include a product the table marks for removal.

The product table is product_table_20260902.xlsx. The duration rules and the approach rules come from the codebook dataDictionary20260828.xlsx. Both files ship with the package, and the tables below read them when the vignette builds, so they cannot disagree with either file. Steps 2 to 5 are the 2026-08-28 layer, reached through that layer’s own dated helpers. Section 1 lists the products the two entry points classify differently, and section 3 verifies that they agree on the fixture. The function’s arguments, the columns it owns and the conditions it rejects are in ?add_lmed_v20260902. This vignette does not repeat them.

product_table <- system.file("2023-mht", "product_table_20260902.xlsx", package = "mht")
codebook <- system.file("2023-mht", "dataDictionary20260828.xlsx", package = "mht")
sheets <- setdiff(readxl::excel_sheets(product_table), "README")
sheets
#> [1] "G"     "other"
ptab <- rbindlist(
  lapply(sheets, function(s) {
    setDT(suppressMessages(readxl::read_excel(product_table, sheet = s, col_types = "text")))
  }),
  use.names = TRUE,
  fill = TRUE
)
ptab[, .N, keyby = .(sheet = fifelse(atc %like% "^G0[23]", "G", "other"))]
#> Key: <sheet>
#>     sheet     N
#>    <char> <int>
#> 1:      G   182
#> 2:  other  2425
groups <- setDT(readxl::read_excel(codebook, sheet = "MHT_groups", col_types = "text"))
groups <- groups[!is.na(Preparatnamn)]

1. Products and categories

How a product name is looked up

The function reduces the register’s product name to its ASCII letters, then lowercases it. Estradot 25, Estradot® and Estradot all become estradot. It then looks that key up in the product table, on an exact match. Extra digits, spaces and symbols disappear in the reduction, so they still match. Extra letters do not: estradotmatrix would match no key. The table holds one row per raw register name, so several rows can share one key. Rows that share a key MUST agree on the category, on the exclusion flag and on its reason. The function errors where they do not.

A delivered name with no row is an error. The function checks the whole prescription table before it restricts to the people in the skeleton. A product held only by people outside the cohort therefore still needs a row. A product nobody has ruled on would otherwise read as no MHT, and its holder would enter as an unexposed control. The table was built from the two register deliveries the studies hold, so a later delivery can bring a name it lacks. The function then stops until the table gains the row.

notmht in the table is a recorded decision that the product is not MHT. A prescription of such a product contributes nothing, and the function reports nothing about it.

The reader validates four things. A category MUST be one the person-week grid materialises, one the 2026-08-28 classifier returns, or notmht. The exclusion cell MUST read TRUE or FALSE. The key MUST equal the raw name reduced, so a key is never trusted. Rows sharing a key MUST agree, as above. No other cell is checked.

The categories

The table names 33 categories, each with at least one product. A category is one letter for the drug group and one number for a subgroup: the route, the progestogen or the regimen. The table below lists every product that reaches each category. The meaning column is the product table’s own English translation of the codebook’s group and route cells, shown without the table’s parenthetical notes. The route is the codebook’s. The lookup reads the product name only, and never checks the route dispensed.

legend <- ptab[classification != "notmht",
  .(
    meaning = paste(unique(sub(" \\(.*\\)$", "", classification_meaning)), collapse = " | "),
    products = paste(unique(produkt_raw), collapse = ", ")
  ),
  keyby = .(category = classification)
]
legend <- legend[order(substr(category, 1, 1), as.integer(substring(category, 2)))]
knitr::kable(legend)
category meaning products

The letter groups the drug. A is oestrogen alone. B is oestrogen with a progestogen in one product. C is a progestogen alone. D, E and I are contraceptive progestogens. F is tibolone, G is a tissue-selective oestrogen complex and H is an androgen. The codebook counts A3, A4 and A5 as local treatment, although A5 is a peroral oestriol. No approach rule treats one of the three as MHT exposure.

What changed against the 2026-08-28 classifier

The 2026-08-28 entry point classifies with a prefix ladder written into the code. The chunk below runs that ladder over every raw name of the G sheet and lists the names where the table answers differently. A ladder answer of none and a table answer of notmht are the same outcome, and are not listed.

compare <- ptab[atc %like% "^G0[23]", .(produkt = produkt_raw, table = classification)]
mht:::lmed_categorize_product_names_v20260828(compare)
compare[, ladder := fifelse(is.na(product_category), "notmht", product_category)]
compare[table != ladder, .(produkt, ladder, table)]
#>                 produkt ladder  table
#>                  <char> <char> <char>
#> 1:       Depo-Progevera notmht     D1
#> 2:              Ceranor notmht     C3
#> 3: Oestriol Imi Pharma® notmht     A5
#> 4:       Oestriol Mylan notmht     A5
#> 5:     Dienogest Besins notmht     C3
#> 6:            Endovelle notmht     C3

Each of these products reached no category under the ladder and reaches one under the table. Endovelle is now a C3 product. In a week it shares with a systemic oestrogen it lights estrogen_progesterone_synthetic, and it keeps estrogen_only from lighting.

Categories that never change exposure

Two categories can be classified and still move no exposure variable, G1 and H1. A third, D4, is a column that no product reaches. A3, A4 and A5 are read only by the inert reference-level rules of section 4, so they move nothing either.

pg <- setDT(suppressMessages(
  readxl::read_excel(codebook, sheet = "post_grouping", col_types = "text")
))
pg <- pg[!is.na(approach)]
ex_cols <- grep("^doesnotinclude", names(pg), value = TRUE)
read <- cat_order(na.omit(unlist(pg[, c("includes1", "includes2", ex_cols), with = FALSE])))
read
#>  [1] "A1"  "A2"  "A3"  "A4"  "A5"  "A6"  "A7"  "B1"  "B2"  "B3"  "B4"  "B5" 
#> [13] "B6"  "B7"  "B8"  "B9"  "B10" "B11" "B12" "C1"  "C2"  "C3"  "C4"  "C5" 
#> [25] "D1"  "D2"  "D3"  "E1"  "F1"  "I1"  "I2"
  • G1 is Duavive alone, and Duavive counts as no MHT. The table gives it G1, and the person-week grid has no G1 column, so no rule can read it.
  • H1 is the androgens. The grid carries an H1 column, and no approach rule names it.
  • D4 appears nowhere in the codebook. The grid carries a D4 column that is FALSE in every week, and no rule names it.

Products whose holders the study removes

The table flags a product with exclude_entire_person. The flag is separate from the category: a flagged product keeps its category, so a reversed exclusion loses nothing. Section 6 states what the function does with the flag.

ptab[exclude_entire_person == "TRUE", .(produkt_raw, classification, exclusion_reason)]

2. From a prescription to an interval

The layer reads five columns of the prescription table: the person identifier, produkt, edatum, fddd, and lnmn where a strength-keyed rule needs it. It reads fddd as a number of days, rounded to a whole day with round(), unless a codebook rule says otherwise.

Four steps run, in this order:

  1. Look the product up, as in section 1.
  2. Overwrite fddd with the codebook’s fixed duration, for the products that carry one.
  3. Drop every prescription with no category, no dispensing date, or no positive duration.
  4. Read the strength from lnmn, and apply the whole-months rules.

Step 2 runs before step 3 because an implant carries no useful dispensed quantity, and the fixed duration supplies one. Step 4 runs after step 3 because a prescription with no duration has no interval, whatever its strength. Reading the strength first would turn a missing lnmn on such a row into an error for nothing.

The duration rules come from the codebook’s MHT_groups sheet, and they are matched by prefix, not by exact key. A rule applies where its codebook name is a prefix of the reduced product name, and the longest such name wins. Utrogestan 100mg Capsules takes the Utrogestan rule. An alias in the duration layer gives Utrogest and Gepretix the Utrogestan rules. Their categories come from the table, where all three are C1. The category lookup and the duration rule are chosen independently, and nothing checks that the rule’s codebook subgroup agrees with the table’s category.

The interval is closed. A prescription dispensed on edatum for d days covers edatum to edatum + d - 1. Both ends convert to an ISO week with cstime::date_to_isoyearweek_c(). Each prescription gets its own interval. Overlapping intervals of one category are unioned, and supply left over at a refill is not carried forward.

Fixed durations 

knitr::kable(groups[!is.na(FDDD), .(Preparatnamn, Subgrupp, FDDD)])
Preparatnamn Subgrupp FDDD
Jadelle D3 1680
Jaydess E1 1008
Kyleena E1 1680
Levosert E1 1680
Levosertone E1 1680
Mirena E1 1680

1680 days is five years of twelve 28-day months. 1008 days is three years of the same months. Jaydess is the one product whose fixed duration differs from the rest of its category. The function reads no removal or replacement date, so a device’s interval runs its full length or ends with follow-up.

Whole months for sparse progestogens

A sequential progestogen is taken on some days of each month. Its fddd counts the days of supply, and a sparse supply covers more calendar time than it has days. For each such product the codebook gives minimum_monthly_dose, the days of supply that make one treatment month, and minimum_months, the months a prescription must reach.

knitr::kable(groups[
  !is.na(minimum_monthly_dose),
  .(Preparatnamn, Subgrupp, minimum_monthly_dose, minimum_months, strength_mg_min, strength_mg_max)
])
Preparatnamn Subgrupp minimum_monthly_dose minimum_months strength_mg_min strength_mg_max
Crinone C1 12 1 NA NA
Cyclogest C1 3.33 3 NA NA
Lutinus C1 8 3 NA NA
Utrogestan C1 28 1 NA 150
Utrogestan C1 12 1 150 NA
Progesteron MIC APL C1 3.33 3 NA NA
Desogestrel C3 4 3 NA NA
Cerazette C3 4 3 NA NA
Azalia C3 4 3 NA NA
Gestrina C3 4 3 NA NA
Velavel C3 4 3 NA NA
Vinelle C3 4 3 NA NA
Zarelle C3 4 3 NA NA
Primolut-Nor C4 4.66 3 NA NA
Provera C4 4 3 NA NA
Orgametril C4 4 3 NA NA
Gestapuran C4 4 3 NA NA
Duphaston C5 12 1 NA NA

The rule rewrites fddd in three steps:

  1. months = floor(fddd / minimum_monthly_dose).
  2. If months < minimum_months, the duration is zero and the prescription is dropped.
  3. Otherwise fddd = months * 28.

A month is 28 days because the codebook says so and the grid counts whole weeks. The result rounds down, never up.

Two Utrogestan rules are keyed on strength. strength_mg_min is inclusive and strength_mg_max is exclusive, so the pair NA, 150 and 150, NA covers every strength once. The strength comes from lnmn, the register’s full product name, which carries the dosage form and the strength. The strength is the last number in lnmn followed by mg, with a comma read as a decimal point. A number followed by mg/ is a concentration and does not count. As soon as a strength-keyed product survives step 3, lnmn is required. A surviving row of it with no readable strength is an error.

The chunk below drives the duration layer with one row per case. The layer is an internal function, so the chunk calls it directly.

cases <- data.table(
  lopnr = 1L,
  produkt = c("Divigel", "Cerazette", "Provera", "Provera", "Utrogestan", "Utrogestan", "Utrogest", "Mirena", "Jaydess"),
  lnmn = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg", "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 200 mg", "Utrogest, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg", NA, NA),
  edatum = as.Date("2020-01-06"),
  fddd = c(90, 28, 28, 8, 30, 30, 30, 1, 1)
)
intervals <- mht:::lmed_durations_v20260902(cases, verbose = FALSE)
#> Warning: 1 of 9 classified prescriptions dropped: 0 with no duration, 1 with a
#> duration that is no positive number of days, 0 with no dispensing date
intervals[, .(produkt, lnmn, fddd, duration_days, start_isoyearweek, stop_isoyearweek)]
#>       produkt                            lnmn  fddd duration_days
#>        <char>                          <char> <num>         <num>
#> 1:    Divigel                            <NA>    90            90
#> 2:  Cerazette                            <NA>   196           196
#> 3:    Provera                            <NA>   196           196
#> 4: Utrogestan Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg    28            28
#> 5: Utrogestan Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 200 mg    56            56
#> 6:   Utrogest   Utrogest, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg    28            28
#> 7:     Mirena                            <NA>  1680          1680
#> 8:    Jaydess                            <NA>  1008          1008
#>    start_isoyearweek stop_isoyearweek
#>               <char>           <char>
#> 1:           2020-02          2020-14
#> 2:           2020-02          2020-29
#> 3:           2020-02          2020-29
#> 4:           2020-02          2020-05
#> 5:           2020-02          2020-09
#> 6:           2020-02          2020-05
#> 7:           2020-02          2024-32
#> 8:           2020-02          2022-40

Divigel has no rule and keeps 90 days. Cerazette and Provera at 28 days of supply reach seven months, which is 196 days. Provera at 8 days of supply reaches two months. The rule needs three, so the prescription is dropped and the warning reports it. Utrogestan 100 mg needs 28 days of supply per month and gets one month. Utrogestan 200 mg needs 12 and gets two. Utrogest 100 mg takes the Utrogestan rule. Mirena and Jaydess take their fixed durations, whatever fddd says.

Dropped prescriptions

A prescription of a notmht product reaches no category and is dropped silently. Every other drop is counted in one aggregate warning, under three causes:

  • no dispensing date
  • no duration
  • a duration that is no positive number of days, which includes a whole-months result of zero

Outside the six fixed-duration products, a missing fddd is never imputed.

3. Person-weeks

The skeleton MUST hold each person’s ISO weeks once each, with no gap between the first and the last. Gap bridging and the three-year rule both count rows, and a row is one elapsed week only under that condition. The function errors otherwise, before it writes anything.

Each of the 33 grid categories gets one logical column. G1 is discarded before this step, and D4 is a column that no product reaches. A week is TRUE for a category where any interval of that category includes at least one day of the week. One day of supply on a Sunday marks that week. The same day plus the Monday marks two weeks. An episode already running at a person’s first week is clipped: it reads as starting in that week. The function counts observed weeks and never reaches behind the first one.

The synthetic fixtures show the result. fake_lmed_2026 holds one Utrogestan user, so lnmn is set for those rows first. It also holds one name, Paracetamol, that exists in no real delivery and so has no row in the product table. That row is removed, or the function stops.

skeleton <- copy(fake_skeleton_mht)
lmed <- copy(fake_lmed_2026)
lmed[, lnmn := NA_character_]
lmed[produkt == "Utrogestan", lnmn := "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg"]
lmed <- lmed[produkt != "Paracetamol"]
add_lmed_v20260902(skeleton, lmed, verbose = FALSE)
#> Warning: 1 of 127 classified prescriptions dropped: 0 with no duration, 1 with
#> a duration that is no positive number of days, 0 with no dispensing date
categories <- grep("^[A-I][0-9]+$", names(skeleton), value = TRUE)
categories
#>  [1] "A1"  "A2"  "A3"  "A4"  "A5"  "A6"  "A7"  "B1"  "B2"  "B3"  "B4"  "B5" 
#> [13] "B6"  "B7"  "B8"  "B9"  "B10" "B11" "B12" "C1"  "C2"  "C3"  "C4"  "C5" 
#> [25] "D1"  "D2"  "D3"  "D4"  "E1"  "F1"  "H1"  "I1"  "I2"
skeleton[, lapply(.SD, sum), .SDcols = categories][, .SD, .SDcols = function(x) x > 0]

The grid materialises 33 categories. Two of them, D4 and H1, are read by no approach rule:

setdiff(categories, read)
#> [1] "D4" "H1"

On this input the two entry points agree on every column they share. The fixture holds none of the products of section 1 that the two classify differently. The 2026-09-02 function adds the two exclusion columns of section 6 and nothing else.

older <- copy(fake_skeleton_mht)
suppressWarnings(add_lmed_v20260828(older, lmed, verbose = FALSE))
shared <- intersect(names(skeleton), names(older))
identical(skeleton[, ..shared], older[, ..shared])
#> [1] TRUE
setdiff(names(skeleton), names(older))
#> [1] "ri_mht_excluded_product" "ri_mht_excluded_reason"

The skeleton must be weekly

swereg::create_skeleton() writes one annual row per person per year before the weekly rows. An annual row holds is_isoyear = TRUE and an isoyearweek that is no ISO week:

id isoyearweek is_isoyear
1 1946-** TRUE
1 2015-02 FALSE

The function stops on the annual row, before it writes anything:

skeleton$isoyearweek holds a value that is no ISO week: 1946-**

Pass the weekly rows only, and fill the annual rows in the caller:

weekly <- skeleton[is_isoyear == FALSE]
add_lmed_v20260902(weekly, lmed)

The subset is a new data.table, so the function writes its columns there.

4. From categories to a treatment level

The post_grouping sheet defines three approaches. Each approach is a set of rules. A rule names one treatment variable, the categories a week must carry, and the categories it must not carry. The rule lights its variable in every week that carries all of the first set and none of the second. Several rules can name one variable, and each lights it on its own.

The tables below compress the rules that name at least one category. alone lists the categories that light the variable on their own. pairs lists the combinations that light it, written as oestrogens + partners. Every oestrogen listed pairs with every partner listed. The chunk asserts that the pairs are exactly that cross, with no pair missing and none repeated. excludes lists the categories a week must not carry. Every rule of one variable carries the same excludes, and the chunk asserts that too.

pg[, excludes := apply(.SD, 1, function(r) paste(cat_order(r[!is.na(r)]), collapse = " ")),
  .SDcols = ex_cols]
rule_table <- function(a) {
  x <- pg[approach == a & !is.na(includes1)]
  out <- x[, {
    alone <- includes1[is.na(includes2)]
    p1 <- includes1[!is.na(includes2)]
    p2 <- includes2[!is.na(includes2)]
    seen <- paste(p1, p2)
    cross <- as.vector(outer(unique(p1), unique(p2), paste))
    stopifnot(anyDuplicated(seen) == 0L, setequal(seen, cross))
    stopifnot(length(unique(excludes)) == 1L)
    .(
      rules = .N,
      alone = paste(cat_order(alone), collapse = " "),
      pairs = if (length(p1) == 0L) "" else
        paste(paste(cat_order(p1), collapse = "/"), "+", paste(cat_order(p2), collapse = "/")),
      excludes = paste(unique(excludes[nzchar(excludes)]), collapse = " | ")
    )
  }, keyby = variable]
  return(out[order(variable == "local_or_none_mht", variable)])
}

Approach 1: any systemic MHT 

knitr::kable(rule_table("1"))
variable rules alone pairs excludes
systemic_mht 16 A1 A2 A6 A7 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12
tibolone 1 F1
local_or_none_mht 3 A3 A4 A5 A1 A2 A6 A7 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12

Every A group systemic oestrogen and every B product is one level, systemic_mht. Tibolone is its own level. No rule of approach 1 reads a progestogen or a contraceptive. A woman on oestrogen with a separate progestogen is systemic_mht. A woman on a progestogen alone is not exposed.

Approach 2: route of the oestrogen 

knitr::kable(rule_table("2"))
variable rules alone pairs excludes
peroral_estrogen 12 A2 A6 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12
tibolone 1 F1
transdermal_estrogen 4 A1 A7 B1 B7
local_or_none_mht 3 A3 A4 A5 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 D1 D2 D3 E1 I1 I2

Approach 2 splits systemic oestrogen by route. Injected oestrogen (A7) sits with the transdermal route. The combined products follow the route of their oestrogen: the two patches, B1 and B7, are transdermal, and the ten tablets are peroral. Tibolone is again its own level.

Approach 3: the progestogen 

knitr::kable(rule_table("3"))
variable rules alone pairs excludes
estrogen_only 4 A1 A2 A6 A7 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 D1 D2 D3 E1 I1 I2
estrogen_progesterone_bioidentical 10 B4 B11 A1/A2/A6/A7 + C1/C5
estrogen_progesterone_synthetic 46 B1 B2 B3 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B12 A1/A2/A6/A7 + C2/C3/C4/D1/D2/D3/E1/I1/I2
tibolone 1 F1

Approach 3 asks what accompanies the oestrogen. estrogen_only is a systemic oestrogen with no combined product, no progestogen and no contraceptive in the same week. The two estrogen_progesterone levels split the progestogen. The codebook’s bioidentical level holds vaginal progesterone (C1) and dydrogesterone (C5, and the combined products B4 and B11). Its synthetic level holds every other progestogen, including injected progesterone (C2), whether in a combined product or dispensed separately. The two names are the codebook’s labels, and this vignette does not judge them. Tibolone is its own level. A progestogen or a contraceptive alone lights nothing.

Approach 3 also declares local_or_none_mht with an empty rule. That rule lights nothing.

The reference level

local_or_none_mht is the value a week takes when no treatment variable is lit. The rules that name it, in every approach, are inert. The resolver never reads the column they light, and it deletes that column with the rest of its working columns. The name says what such a week holds: a local oestrogen, a progestogen alone, a contraceptive, an androgen, Duavive, or nothing.

Bridging a gap

Before the resolver compares treatment variables, it bridges short gaps in each of them separately. For one variable, a run of up to four weeks in which it is unlit, between two weeks in which it is lit, becomes lit. A leading or a trailing run is not a gap, so no woman starts early and none stops late. The category columns are not bridged: bridging happens inside the approach step.

skel <- toy_skeleton()
add_lmed_v20260902(skel, rbind(rx("Divigel", 1, 10), rx("Divigel", 14, 7)), verbose = FALSE)
episodes(skel, "approach1")
#>       id    from      to weeks             level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>            <char>
#> 1:     1 2020-02 2020-21    20      systemic_mht
#> 2:     1 2020-22 2020-41    20 local_or_none_mht
skel <- toy_skeleton()
add_lmed_v20260902(skel, rbind(rx("Divigel", 1, 10), rx("Divigel", 16, 5)), verbose = FALSE)
episodes(skel, "approach1")
#>       id    from      to weeks             level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>            <char>
#> 1:     1 2020-02 2020-11    10      systemic_mht
#> 2:     1 2020-12 2020-16     5 local_or_none_mht
#> 3:     1 2020-17 2020-21     5      systemic_mht
#> 4:     1 2020-22 2020-41    20 local_or_none_mht

A three-week gap is bridged. A five-week gap is not, and the woman holds two episodes.

One level per week: the most recent start wins

A week can light two treatment variables. Concomitance is judged at ISO-week resolution, so two products dispensed on different days of one week count as concomitant. The resolver gives each variable a run length, which counts the weeks since it last turned on, and reports the variable with the shortest run. The treatment the woman started most recently is the one reported.

The woman below takes Progynon (A2) for 30 weeks and adds Divigel (A1) from week 11 for 20 weeks.

skel <- toy_skeleton()
add_lmed_v20260902(skel, rbind(rx("Progynon", 1, 30), rx("Divigel", 11, 20)), verbose = FALSE)
episodes(skel, "approach1")
#>       id    from      to weeks             level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>            <char>
#> 1:     1 2020-02 2020-31    30      systemic_mht
#> 2:     1 2020-32 2020-41    10 local_or_none_mht
episodes(skel, "approach2")
#>       id    from      to weeks                level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>               <char>
#> 1:     1 2020-02 2020-11    10     peroral_estrogen
#> 2:     1 2020-12 2020-31    20 transdermal_estrogen
#> 3:     1 2020-32 2020-41    10    local_or_none_mht
episodes(skel, "approach3")
#>       id    from      to weeks             level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>            <char>
#> 1:     1 2020-02 2020-31    30     estrogen_only
#> 2:     1 2020-32 2020-41    10 local_or_none_mht

Approach 1 sees one level throughout, because A1 and A2 are both systemic_mht. Approach 2 reports peroral_estrogen for ten weeks and then transdermal_estrogen, the more recent start, for twenty. Approach 3 sees estrogen_only throughout.

An exclusion works the same way. The woman below takes Divigel for 20 weeks and Utrogestan 100 mg from week 9 for 8 weeks.

skel <- toy_skeleton()
add_lmed_v20260902(
  skel,
  rbind(rx("Divigel", 1, 20), rx("Utrogestan", 9, 8, "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg")),
  verbose = FALSE
)
episodes(skel, "approach3")
#>       id    from      to weeks                              level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>                             <char>
#> 1:     1 2020-02 2020-09     8                      estrogen_only
#> 2:     1 2020-10 2020-17     8 estrogen_progesterone_bioidentical
#> 3:     1 2020-18 2020-21     4                      estrogen_only
#> 4:     1 2020-22 2020-41    20                  local_or_none_mht

While C1 is in force, estrogen_only is not lit, because its rule excludes C1, and estrogen_progesterone_bioidentical is lit by the pair A1 + C1. When the progesterone ends, estrogen_only lights again. Its eight-week gap is over four weeks, so it is not bridged, and the run restarts.

Two starts in one week: a clash

Two treatment variables that start in the same week have equal run lengths, and neither wins. The week is marked clashingprescriptions. The mark carries forward to the last treated week of that episode, and no further. The first untreated week after it is an ordinary stop.

skel <- toy_skeleton()
add_lmed_v20260902(skel, rbind(rx("Progynon", 1, 30), rx("Divigel", 1, 20)), verbose = FALSE)
episodes(skel, "approach2")
#>       id    from      to weeks                 level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>                <char>
#> 1:     1 2020-02 2020-31    30 clashingprescriptions
#> 2:     1 2020-32 2020-41    10     local_or_none_mht

Neither end of that rule is arbitrary. A clash carried to the end of follow-up would keep a woman who stopped and restarted out of the comparison for good. A clash ended with the overlap would read her as a new user in the week the overlap ends, and she was treated throughout.

5. The exposure variables

The exposure layer turns each approach column into two exposure columns, rd_approach<N>_single and rd_approach<N>_multiple. Each holds the approach’s levels, clashingprescriptions among them, plus two more: previous and exclude. Five steps run per approach and per variant:

  1. Mark the move from an active level to local_or_none_mht as previous. Every later untreated week is also previous.
  2. Find the first week that moves from previous back to an active level. That is the re-initiation.
  3. In the single variant only, set every week from the re-initiation onward to exclude.
  4. Rewrite previous to exclude where the treated episode before it ran under 156 weeks, which is three years of 52.
  5. Write the result.

clashingprescriptions counts as an active level in every step. A woman who leaves a clash for no treatment is a former user like any other.

The single variant allows one treated episode in the observed follow-up. Everything from a second start onward leaves the analysis. A start before the first observed week is not seen, so the first observed episode counts as the first. The multiple variant lets her re-enter her new level, and excludes person-time only through step 4.

Former user or excluded

Two women in the fixture stop and never restart. Person 1 was treated for 193 weeks, person 2 for 73.

episodes(skeleton[id %in% c(1, 2)], "rd_approach3_single")
#>       id    from      to weeks         level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>        <char>
#> 1:     1 2015-02 2018-37   193 estrogen_only
#> 2:     1 2018-38 2020-52   119      previous
#> 3:     2 2015-02 2016-21    73 estrogen_only
#> 4:     2 2016-22 2020-52   239       exclude

Person 1 becomes previous, a former user. Person 2 becomes exclude, because 73 weeks is under 156. Every week before a woman’s first treatment stays local_or_none_mht.

Re-initiation, single against multiple

Person 6 was treated for 193 weeks, stopped for 21, and restarted for 50.

episodes(skeleton[id == 6], "rd_approach3_single")
#>       id    from      to weeks         level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>        <char>
#> 1:     6 2015-02 2018-37   193 estrogen_only
#> 2:     6 2018-38 2019-06    21      previous
#> 3:     6 2019-07 2020-52    98       exclude
episodes(skeleton[id == 6], "rd_approach3_multiple")
#>       id    from      to weeks         level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>        <char>
#> 1:     6 2015-02 2018-37   193 estrogen_only
#> 2:     6 2018-38 2019-06    21      previous
#> 3:     6 2019-07 2020-04    50 estrogen_only
#> 4:     6 2020-05 2020-52    48       exclude

In the single variant, the 21 untreated weeks are previous, because the first episode reached 156 weeks, and every week from the restart is exclude. In the multiple variant she re-enters estrogen_only for 50 weeks. Her final untreated weeks are exclude, because that second episode ran under 156 weeks.

Approach 3b

rd_approach3b_single and rd_approach3b_multiple are the approach 3 columns with the two estrogen_progesterone levels collapsed into one. A switch between active levels never creates previous, so the relabel gives what a full second pass would give.

episodes(skeleton[id == 16], "rd_approach3_single")
#>       id    from      to weeks                           level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>                          <char>
#> 1:    16 2015-02 2016-21    73 estrogen_progesterone_synthetic
#> 2:    16 2016-22 2020-52   239                         exclude
episodes(skeleton[id == 16], "rd_approach3b_single")
#>       id    from      to weeks                 level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>                <char>
#> 1:    16 2015-02 2016-21    73 estrogen_progesterone
#> 2:    16 2016-22 2020-52   239               exclude

6. The exclusion flags

ri_mht_excluded_product is TRUE in every week of a person whose supplied prescriptions include a flagged product, and FALSE otherwise. ri_mht_excluded_reason carries the table’s reason, or NA. Where one person holds products flagged for different reasons, the reasons join in sorted order, separated by ;.

The flag is set from holding the product. It does not depend on that prescription having a usable duration or a dispensing date, and it does not depend on the week. A flagged prescription dispensed before or after follow-up flags every observed week all the same. The prescriptions the caller passes therefore define the window of ascertainment. The ri_ prefix means person level and time invariant.

The function removes nobody. It reports. A flagged person keeps every exposure column, computed as for anyone else, and the caller decides what to do with her rows.

skeleton[, .N, keyby = .(ri_mht_excluded_product, ri_mht_excluded_reason)]
#> Key: <ri_mht_excluded_product, ri_mht_excluded_reason>
#>    ri_mht_excluded_product            ri_mht_excluded_reason     N
#>                     <lgcl>                            <char> <int>
#> 1:                   FALSE                              <NA>  5304
#> 2:                    TRUE possible gender-affirming therapy   312
flagged <- skeleton[ri_mht_excluded_product == TRUE, unique(id)]
lmed[lopnr %in% flagged, .(lopnr, produkt, edatum, fddd)]
#>    lopnr       produkt     edatum  fddd
#>    <int>        <char>     <Date> <num>
#> 1:     8       Divigel 2015-01-05    28
#> 2:     8      Progynon 2015-03-31    28
#> 3:     8       Vagifem 2015-06-20    28
#> 4:     8       Blissel 2015-09-11    28
#> 5:     8 Oestriolaspen 2015-12-08    28
#> 6:     8     Premarina 2016-02-29    28
#> 7:     8     Neofollin 2016-05-23    28
episodes(skeleton[id %in% flagged], "approach1")
#>       id    from      to weeks             level
#>    <int>  <char>  <char> <int>            <char>
#> 1:     8 2015-02 2015-05     4      systemic_mht
#> 2:     8 2015-06 2015-13     8 local_or_none_mht
#> 3:     8 2015-14 2015-18     5      systemic_mht
#> 4:     8 2015-19 2016-08    43 local_or_none_mht
#> 5:     8 2016-09 2016-12     4      systemic_mht
#> 6:     8 2016-13 2016-20     8 local_or_none_mht
#> 7:     8 2016-21 2016-24     4      systemic_mht
#> 8:     8 2016-25 2020-52   236 local_or_none_mht

Person 8 holds one Neofollin prescription among six others. Every one of her 312 weeks is flagged, and her approach columns are still written.

7. What the function does not do

  • It removes no person. The exclusion flag is the caller’s to act on.
  • It reads no diagnosis and no covariate. The codebook’s diagnosis-based exclusion is not applied. The table instead flags products whose holders the study removes.
  • It builds no history before a woman’s first observed week. A prescription dispensed before that week still covers the weeks of it inside follow-up, and the episode reads as starting in the first observed week.
  • It imputes no duration, outside the six fixed-duration products. Any other prescription with no usable fddd contributes nothing.
  • It reads the Rules, FDDD and covariates sheets of the codebook, and the README sheet of the product table, not at all.
